Well, there are families of games like Samurai Warriors, Dynasty Warriors, etc. that all follow different stories based on different themes. Dynasty warriors follows the story of the romance of the three kingdoms, with three major factions vying for conquest. While each game has several mini-campaigns for each faction (and sometimes each character), the any dynasty warriors game will have the exact same story as its predecessor.

There are some notable exceptions to this, such as warriors orochi (with subsequent games continuing the story rather than restarting it), and anime tie-ins like that one piece game, or gundam warriors.

Dynasty Warriors is one of those franchises that impresses me with their success. Not because they're bad games, but because they haven't really mixed up the formula much since the first game. It's still the same relative gameplay, the same story, the same characters, co-op modes and campaign. It's impressive that a company has remained successful while still staying true to the same formula they've used for fifteen years.

It truly is the COD of ancient third person combat games. Just incremental updates and tweaks on the same game. It is a guilty pleasure and I wish I still had a console with which to play it.
